verses.text: Then all Israel gathered themselves to David to Hebron, saying, “Behold, we are your bone and your flesh.

In times past, even when Saul was king, it was you who led out and brought in Israel. Yahweh your God said to you, ‘You shall be shepherd of my people Israel, and you shall be prince over my people Israel.’”
So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and David made a covenant with them in Hebron before Yahweh; and they anointed David king over Israel, according to Yahweh’s word by Samuel.
David and all Israel went to Jerusalem (also called Jebus); and the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were there.
The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, “You will not come in here.” Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion. The same is David’s city.
David said, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites first shall be chief and captain.” Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first, and was made chief.
David lived in the stronghold; therefore they called it David’s city.
He built the city all around, from Millo even around; and Joab repaired the rest of the city.
David grew greater and greater; for Yahweh of Armies was with him.

Now these are the chief of the mighty men whom David had, who showed themselves strong with him in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to Yahweh’s word concerning Israel.
This is the number of the mighty men whom David had: Jashobeam, the son of a Hachmonite, the chief of the thirty; he lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed them at one time.
After him was Eleazar the son of Dodo, the Ahohite, who was one of the three mighty men.
He was with David at Pasdammim, and there the Philistines were gathered together to battle, where there was a plot of ground full of barley; and the people fled from before the Philistines.
They stood in the middle of the plot, defended it, and killed the Philistines; and Yahweh saved them by a great victory.
Three of the thirty chief men went down to the rock to David, into the cave of Adullam; and the army of the Philistines were encamped in the valley of Rephaim.
David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was in Bethlehem at that time.
David longed, and said, “Oh that one would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate!”

The three broke through the army of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David; but David would not drink any of it, but poured it out to Yahweh,

and said, “My God forbid me, that I should do this! Shall I drink the blood of these men who have put their lives in jeopardy?” For they risked their lives to bring it. Therefore he would not drink it. The three mighty men did these things.
Abishai, the brother of Joab, he was chief of the three; for he lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed them, and had a name among the three.
Of the three, he was more honorable than the two, and was made their captain; however he wasn’t included in the three.

Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done mighty deeds, killed the two sons of Ariel of Moab. He also went down and killed a lion in the middle of a pit on a snowy day.

He killed an Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits  high. In the Egyptian’s hand was a spear like a weaver’s beam; and he went down to him with a staff, plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did these things, and had a name among the three mighty men.
Behold, he was more honorable than the thirty, but he didn’t attain to the three; and David set him over his guard.
The mighty men of the armies also include Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,
Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite,
Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,
Maharai the Netophathite, Heled the son of Baanah the Netophathite,
Ithai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite,
Hurai of the brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,
Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,
the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan the son of Shagee the Hararite,
Ahiam the son of Sacar the Hararite, Eliphal the son of Ur,
Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,
Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai the son of Ezbai,
Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar the son of Hagri,
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, the armor bearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah,
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite, Zabad the son of Ahlai,
Adina the son of Shiza the Reubenite, a chief of the Reubenites, and thirty with him,
Hanan the son of Maacah, and Joshaphat the Mithnite,
Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,
Jediael the son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite,
Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai, and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite,
Eliel, and Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.

footnotes.content: All Israel gathers to David at Hebron, saying 'we are your bone and your flesh.' There's a tender recognition here—they see him not as a distant ruler, but as kin. The Lord draws a scattered people together around one shepherd.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The people recall that even under Saul, David was the real shepherd—he led out and brought in Israel. They cite Yahweh's word to David: shepherd and prince. The Lord's claim on us often comes before the world sees it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the elders come to Hebron and make covenant with David before Yahweh, then anoint him king—fulfilling Samuel's anointing years before. Covenant-making in God's sight seals what has long been promised.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David and all Israel go to Jerusalem (Jebus), where the Jebusites still hold the city. To take the seat of kingship, he must enter the enemy's stronghold. Sometimes the Lord's calling takes us into places we must contest in faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Jebusites boast: 'You will not come in here.' But David takes the stronghold of Zion. What seemed impossible falls when we move in the Lord's name—and becomes known ever after as David's city.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David offers chief command to whoever strikes the Jebusites first. Joab rises first and is made chief. Sometimes honor goes to the one willing to lead—to step first through the breach, not wait for a safer path.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David lives in the stronghold, and it is called by his name. A place is marked by who dwells there, who claims it. When we belong to Jesus, His name marks us too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He builds the city all around, from Millo even around; Joab repairs the rest. City-building is not one man's work alone—Joab's faithfulness complements David's vision. The Lord builds His kingdom through the loyalty of many.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David grew greater and greater, for Yahweh of Armies was with him. All the building, all the victories—their source is not David's strength but the Lord's presence. We grow great only as we abide in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: These are the chief of the mighty men who showed themselves strong with David in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king according to Yahweh's word. The roster that follows is not mere names—each one is a testimony to courage shown together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jashobeam, the son of a Hachmonite, chief of the thirty; he lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed them at one time. A man of singular valor—he stands alone and prevails. The Lord gives strength beyond what we measure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After Jashobeam comes Eleazar, son of Dodo, the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men. Each man named carries a name, a lineage, a place—each one seen and counted. The Lord misses no faithful servant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eleazar was with David at Pasdammim, where the Philistines gathered to battle on a plot of barley, and the people fled. He stood his ground when fear scattered others. Sometimes faithfulness looks like standing alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They stood in the middle of the plot, defended it, and killed the Philistines; Yahweh saved them by a great victory. Eleazar and his companion held the ground—not by their strength alone, but by the Lord's salvation breaking through.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three of the thirty chief men went down to the rock to David into the cave of Adullam, while the army of the Philistines camped in the valley of Rephaim. Even in exile, even hiding in a cave, David draws faithful men. The faithful know where to find their shepherd.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem. His city is held by the enemy. Yet his loyal men go even there—into danger—because love for their king outweighs fear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David longed and said, 'Oh that one would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate!' A longing for home, for the familiar place of his youth. Even kings know homesickness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The three broke through the Philistine army, drew water from Bethlehem's well by the gate, and brought it to David; but David poured it out to Yahweh. He would not drink what his friends risked their lives to bring—not out of rudeness, but reverence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David said, 'My God forbid me, that I should do this! Shall I drink the blood of these men who have put their lives in jeopardy?' He could not drink the price of their blood. True leadership honors the cost borne by those faithful to it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abishai, the brother of Joab, was chief of the three; he lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed them, and had a name among the three. Like Jashobeam, a man of singular valor—kinship and courage often walk together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Of the three, Abishai was more honorable than the two and was made their captain; however he wasn't included in the three. A paradox: honored above, yet not of that innermost circle. Service sometimes means seeing others exalted above you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, from Kabzeel, had done mighty deeds—he killed two sons of Ariel of Moab and a lion in a pit on a snowy day. A man of varied courage, testing his strength against both foe and beast. The Lord's men are many-gifted.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Benaiah killed an Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits high, whose spear was like a weaver's beam. Benaiah went down with a staff, plucked the spear from the giant's hand, and killed him with his own spear. Faith often means stepping into the face of the feared.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, did these things and had a name among the three mighty men. His courage earned him a place among the legendary. The Lord remembers every act of faithful strength.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He was more honorable than the thirty, but he didn't attain to the three; David set him over his guard. Again, the paradox—honor and yet not the innermost circle. His faithfulness fitted him to protect the king, a noble charge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The mighty men of the armies include Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan of Bethlehem. The roster grows; brothers stand side by side. Loyalty often runs in families.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite. Names and places recorded—each one seen in the sight of God and history. No faithful servant is ever truly forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ira the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite. Men of the countryside, their towns named beside their names. The Lord draws warriors from every place, city and village alike.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite. Two more names carried forward. Each man answering the call, each one counted.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Maharai the Netophathite, Heled the son of Baanah the Netophathite. Even their hometowns are honored in the record. A man's place shapes his story, and the Lord honors both.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ithai of Gibeah of Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite. From tribe to town, the faithful gather. Unity comes not from sameness but from sharing one shepherd.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hurai of the brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite. Even the brooks are named—these men are known in their homeland, and their allegiance carries them far beyond it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite. Names continuing to echo—each one witnessed, each one treasured in the chronicle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan, son of Shagee the Hararite. Families serve together, lineages honored. The Lord builds His work through generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ahiam the Hararite, Eliphal the son of Ur. More names, more places, more witnesses to faithfulness. The roll goes on—each one seen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite. The naming continues, unhurried and thorough—as if the chronicler says: 'Each one matters. I will not skip.'
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai the son of Ezbai. From different lands they come, Carmel and beyond. One king draws the faithful to him from every direction.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar the son of Hagri. More brothers, more sons—lineages and ties preserved. These are not abstract warriors, but men with families who knew them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, the armor bearer of Joab. Even those from other nations stand here—an Ammonite counted among David's mighty men. The Lord's grace crosses all borders.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite. Two men from the same place, standing together. Hometown bonds often hold firm.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Uriah the Hittite, Zabad the son of Ahlai. Here Uriah is named among David's mightiest, before tragedy will mark his story. In this moment, he stands honored—a faithful warrior, a faithful husband. The Lord sees him whole.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Adina the son of Shiza the Reubenite, a chief of the Reubenites, and thirty with him. A leader who brings others with him—thirty men follow Adina's loyalty. Such men multiply the kingdom's strength.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hanan the son of Maacah, Joshaphat the Mithnite. Two more standing in the roll of honor. Each one adds to the treasury of faithful hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite. More brothers, more places, more names carried forward to eternity. God's memory is perfect.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jediael the son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite. Again brothers stand together—loyalty runs deep when it runs in families.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eliel the Mahavite, Jeribai and Joshaviah the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite. A Moabite counted here too—another outsider grafted into David's covenant loyalty. The Lord's kingdom transcends all earthly division.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eliel, Obed, Jaasiel the Mezobaite. The roll ends, the names complete—and readers today hear an echo in this: that Jesus too keeps the names of His faithful, writes them in His book, and will call them by name when He welcomes us home. No one faithful is ever forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
